title: Irregular line past recap; the irregular dot-past group: tuve, estuve, dije

cards.title: Line past: only three irregulars
cards.body: Ser → era (an era), ir → iba (-aba + -ía), ver → veía (keeps veo's e). Everything else is regular.

examples.en: we were / they were going / they were seeing

cards.title: The irregular dot-past group
cards.body: Mostly -go verbs. Three features: a changed stem (pod- → pud-); a fixed mix of endings (-e and -o from the -ar set, the rest from -er/-ir); and no stress on the endings.

cards.title: tener → tuv-
cards.body: Tuve, tuvo (unstressed endings, from -ar), then tuvimos, tuviste, tuvieron (from -er/-ir).

examples.en: I had / he had / we had / you had / they had
Where were you? / Where were you guys?

cards.title: Escape hatch: the line past
cards.body: In a live conversation, the regular line past (¿dónde estabas?, tenía que ir) gets the meaning across. Don't avoid the irregulars forever, though: whatever you don't take control of ends up controlling you.

examples.en: I had to go (at that moment).
examples.es: Tuve que ir. / Tenía que ir.

examples.en: I said / he said / we said
